claim: EngramEdit demonstrates that a frozen conditional-memory table can be edited without touching the backbone, by keeping the pretrained hashed tables fixed and storing a separate cumulative update vector per edited n-gram indexed by its exact token sequence.
stance_target: The viability of frozen Engram tables as a stable substrate
scope_conditions: LongCat-Flash-Lite 68.5B MoE with 31.4B n-gram embedding parameters, two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs
quoted_support: Each vector is added to the embedding output whenever its n-gram is activated, while the pretrained tables remain fixed.

claim: EngramEdit achieves near-perfect editing success on CounterFact and ZsRE by updating only conditional memory, with generalization to unseen expressions and multi-hop reasoning at nearly 3x the strongest baseline's accuracy.
stance_target: Whether frozen memory can be a knowledge-update interface
scope_conditions: 2,000 edits in batches of 100, extended to 5,000 facts; MQuAKE 3,000 cases
quoted_support: By updating only conditional memory, EngramEdit achieves near-perfect editing success on both CounterFact and ZsRE... with nearly 3x the strongest baseline's accuracy under [multi-hop reasoning].

claim: The EngramEdit substrate stores 31.4B of 68.5B parameters in n-gram embeddings - about 46% of total parameters are memory rather than compute.
stance_target: How large a fraction of a production model can be frozen memory
quoted_support: All experiments use LongCat-Flash-Lite, a 68.5B-parameter MoE model with 31.4B parameters in n-gram embeddings.

claim: LongCat-Flash-Lite's conditional memory uses suffix n-grams of length 2, 3, and 4 with four hashed sub-tables per length, each returning a 256-dimensional vector projected to the 3,072-dimensional token embedding space, averaged with the token embedding at each position.
stance_target: The concrete table geometry of a production Engram-style memory
quoted_support: Its conditional memory uses suffix n-grams of lengths 2, 3, and 4, with four hashed sub-tables per length. Each sub-table returns a 256-dimensional vector, which is linearly projected to the 3,072-dimensional token embedding space.

claim: Disabling Engram memory in a DeepSeek Engram model causes larger relative performance drops on factual-knowledge benchmarks than on other categories, confirming memory holds parametric knowledge.
stance_target: The functional split between memory and backbone
scope_conditions: DeepSeek Engram ablation cited by EngramEdit
quoted_support: Disabling memory in DeepSeek Engram causes larger relative performance drops on factual-knowledge benchmarks.

claim: Editing cost scales with the number of distinct edited n-grams rather than table size, and exact indexing prevents hash collisions from coupling updates.
stance_target: Whether frozen-table edits stay cheap as the table grows
quoted_support: Editing only requires storing updates for the selected n-grams. We therefore maintain a separate cumulative update vector for each edited n-gram, indexed by its exact token sequence. Additional storage scales with the number of distinct edited n-grams, and the exact indexing prevents hash collisions from coupling their updates.

claim: The joint update objective provably minimizes weighted embedding update cost among all updates producing the same target representations, with stronger penalties on frequently reused embeddings to preserve unrelated knowledge.
stance_target: Whether memory edits can be made surgical rather than destructive
scope_conditions: EngramEdit weighted least-squares formulation with ridge and reuse regularization
quoted_support: EngramEdit minimizes the weighted embedding update cost among all updates [producing the same targets]... the bound assigns a larger cost to the same embedding update when its n-gram is activated [more frequently].

claim: EngramEdit's experiments run on two RTX PRO 6000 GPUs, i.e. a workstation-class 2-GPU setup, showing that a 68.5B model with 31.4B frozen memory parameters can be manipulated on non-datacenter hardware.
stance_target: Whether large frozen-memory models are operable on modest GPU counts
quoted_support: All experiments use LongCat-Flash-Lite, a 68.5B-parameter MoE model with 31.4B parameters in n-gram embeddings, and run on two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs.

claim: EngramEdit is an inference-time knowledge-editing method, not a training method: it never updates the backbone or the pretrained tables, so it provides no evidence about training topology or distributed training cost.
stance_target: Whether EngramEdit evidence bears on training feasibility
quoted_support: EngramEdit keeps the token embeddings and these projection matrices fixed... while all decoder parameters remain fixed.
